classification.difficultyReason: Establish similarity from parallel sides, then combine a corresponding-side ratio with segment addition to prove an identity.

content.prompt: $ABCD$ is a trapezium with $AB\parallel DC$ and $AB=\frac{1}{3}DC$. The diagonals of this trapezium intersect at $O$.

spec.description: Unshaded trapezium with short horizontal upper side AB and longer horizontal lower side DC, with matching parallel arrows. As in the source, diagonals and O are not drawn. Ordinary source blue geometry is rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: AB is parallel to DC and has one third its length; vertices occur in order A, B, C, D.

children.prompt: Prove that $\triangle ABO$ is similar to $\triangle CDO$.

answer.short:
$\triangle ABO\sim\triangle CDO$ (AAA).

Two pairs of alternate angles are equal because $AB\parallel DC$.
answer.worked:
In $\triangle ABO$ and $\triangle CDO$,
$$\angle BAO=\angle DCO\quad\text{(alternate angles, }AB\parallel DC\text{)},$$
$$\angle ABO=\angle CDO\quad\text{(alternate angles, }AB\parallel DC\text{)}.$$
Therefore $\triangle ABO\sim\triangle CDO$ (AAA).

Matching sides of the similar triangles give
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AO}{OC}&=\frac{AB}{CD}\\\frac{AO}{OC}&=\frac{1}{3}\\AO&=\frac{1}{3}OC.\end{align*}$$
Since $O$ lies on $AC$,
$$\begin{align*}AC&=AO+OC\\AC&=\frac{1}{3}OC+OC\\AC&=\frac{4}{3}OC\\3AC&=4OC.\end{align*}$$
